title: The game begins at the draft
description: Twenty-plus players enter with very different levels of fantasy-football experience, a fresh set of NFL rosters, and three tribes that must learn to balance teamwork with self-preservation.

story.heading: Three tribes, competing priorities
story.body: Red, Blue, and Yellow approach the draft with different roster strategies and different social starting points. Quarterback scarcity, lineup balance, and the possibility of trading players become early discussion points. At the same time, the Survivor game is underway: players are building relationships before they know which tribe will be in danger first.

story.heading: More than one early alliance
story.body: The confessional notes capture several overlapping efforts to establish trust. Harry, Justin, Mark, and Aly feature in one set of early conversations; Cody and Nick develop a connection, while Navi and Julia work to find their footing. On Red, smaller groups form around Joel, Allix, Katie, Steve, and others. None of these early arrangements guarantees control once NFL games begin.

story.heading: Advantages change the equation
story.body: Players also have to learn a separate economy of game currency and advantages. Information can move between tribes through special opportunities, even while ordinary cross-tribe communication is restricted. The opening weeks are as much about understanding the rules and other players as they are about scoring fantasy points.

title: Will is the first to go
description: The first NFL results send Red to Tribal, where Will becomes the first player voted out. Elsewhere, the opening scores and new social connections begin to reshape expectations.

story.heading: The first football test
story.body: The season moves from draft projections to actual NFL production. Some teams have assembled reliable starters; others are dependent on riskier combinations or advantages. Results determine who must face a vote, but they do not tell that tribe whom to eliminate.

story.heading: A first Tribal
story.body: Red votes out Will at the opening Tribal Council. It is the first demonstration that fantasy performance and social protection are different kinds of safety. Players on every tribe can now see that an early misread of relationships may matter just as much as a disappointing Sunday lineup.

story.heading: The Edge remains
story.body: An elimination does not necessarily mean the last appearance of a player. Edge of Extinction makes the early vote consequential without making it fully final, and surviving players have to consider whom they might face again.

title: Julia and Jason fall
description: Two tribes visit Tribal and Julia and Jason are eliminated. Their exits come amid competing alliances, football roster decisions, and changing ideas about who is actually vulnerable.

story.heading: Pressure across the beaches
story.body: The second week sends two of the three tribes to Tribal. Immunity outcomes and special advantages affect the available choices, while some players consider whether improving a teammate’s roster might make the whole tribe safer.

story.heading: Conflicting social maps
story.body: Early confessionals show several factions testing trust rather than following a single agreed plan. Justin and Harry weigh their connections with Mark and Aly; Cody, Nick, Navi, John, Braga, and Brian are also sorting out whom to rely on. Suspicion around possible targets does not always match the votes that ultimately land.

story.heading: Two departures, many consequences
story.body: Julia and Jason leave this round. Their eliminations affect separate networks of relationships and leave the remaining players reassessing both their alliances and which advantages are still in circulation.

title: Cody out, Ross departs
description: Cody is voted out, while Ross leaves the game for personal reasons. The changes reach beyond their immediate tribes as the cast looks ahead to a reshuffle.

story.heading: An exit at Tribal and a departure away from it
story.body: Cody is eliminated through the vote. Ross leaves for personal reasons, creating a second change to the cast that cannot be explained by Tribal strategy or fantasy points. Each loss affects the people who had been working with them.

story.heading: Old plans become less reliable
story.body: Across the original tribes, players have been negotiating alliances, comparing advantages, and trying to control weekly lineups. The departures disrupt those assumptions at the same time that a swap looms, making permanent tribal majorities increasingly difficult to count on.

story.heading: An unfinished Edge story
story.body: Eliminated players remain relevant through Edge of Extinction. For those still in the game, the possibility of returnees complicates any decision based on supposedly settled numbers.

title: Brian and Laura are voted out
description: A September 30 tribe swap mixes former allies and rivals into new groups. Brian and Laura are voted out as everyone adapts to unfamiliar teammates and new scoring pressures.

story.heading: The tribe swap redraws the map
story.body: Old color lines no longer guarantee protection. The new groups contain people with separate social histories, competing priorities, and different roster strengths. Some former allies reunite, while others need to establish trust with players they barely know.

story.heading: Everyone has a new calculation
story.body: The swap introduces immediate questions: who can cooperate on fantasy matchups, whose roster can absorb a trade, and whether a previously close relationship is now a threat to a new majority. One new Reba group is selected by Steve, but the reshuffle changes the game for every tribe, not just that one.

story.heading: Two players leave
story.body: Brian and Laura are voted out in the first swapped-tribe round. Their exits show how little security a player can assume after reassignment, especially when social bonds and football scoring are pulling in different directions.

title: The Edge changes the board
description: Nick is voted out, but Edge of Extinction returns Cody and Brian to active play. The reshuffled tribes have to absorb two players whose stories were supposed to be over.

story.heading: The Edge opens again
story.body: Cody and Brian return from Edge of Extinction. The comeback gives them another opportunity to compete and creates uncertainty for players who had been treating earlier departures as settled.

story.heading: Relationships do not reset
story.body: Returnees bring information, old allegiances, and possible grievances into tribes already negotiating their own arrangements. Meanwhile, the original groups have been fragmented by the swap. Long-standing trust may help a player reconnect, but it does not make a new majority automatic.

story.heading: Nick leaves
story.body: Nick is voted out during the same week. His departure and the two returns mean the cast changes in several directions at once, reinforcing how quickly the social and football sides of the game can diverge.

title: Yellow and Blue face Tribal
description: Both Yellow and Blue face Tribal, with Joseph and Mardie eliminated. Their separate paths underline how differently the surviving tribes have evolved.

story.heading: Two Tribals, two sets of relationships
story.body: Yellow and Blue each have to make a decision. By this point, their players have navigated shifting alliances, public advantages, and the ongoing pressure to field a competitive fantasy lineup. What looks like a safe plan from one conversation may not look the same to another group.

story.heading: Longer-term loyalties meet a short-term vote
story.body: The remaining players are also looking toward a merge, when previously separated groups will finally be able to compare their accounts. That prospect increases the value of relationships and information even for players who are not at this week’s Tribal.

story.heading: The field narrows
story.body: Joseph and Mardie are eliminated. Their exits close two individual pre-merge stories while leaving open how the surviving former tribal relationships will carry into the next stage.

title: The tribes converge
description: Brian and Braga leave shortly before the merge. As the remaining players come together, the game changes from protecting a tribe to surviving one shared vote.

story.heading: The last separate votes
story.body: The pre-merge game ends with Brian and Braga leaving at their respective Tribals. Each tribe has arrived here through a different mix of challenge results, strategic relationships, and roster management.

story.heading: New conversations, old histories
story.body: The merge opens communication across the full remaining field. Players begin checking what they had been told about the other tribes, identifying new partners, and discovering that different people experienced the same events very differently.

story.heading: A new kind of vulnerability
story.body: There is now a single voting pool. A strong fantasy team still matters, but no player can rely solely on the connections that protected them on an individual beach. The merger creates opportunities for new coalitions as well as new targets.

title: Mark becomes the first merge casualty
description: Mark becomes the first merged Tribal elimination. As the cast adjusts to one voting group, new agreements emerge across the former tribal lines, including a four-player alliance later called JANS.

story.heading: The first full-cast vote
story.body: Mark is eliminated in the opening merged Tribal. The vote tests whether players can turn pre-merge relationships into support in a much larger group, and it gives everyone new information about where trust and influence may lie.

story.heading: Several routes through the merge
story.body: The post-merge cast is not divided cleanly into two sides. Friendships from Blue, Yellow, and Red overlap with fresh conversations, and players must decide whether to hold to old allies or make new commitments. Public events and reward outcomes provide fresh reasons for people to cooperate.

story.heading: One alliance among several
story.body: On November 1, Joel, Aly, Navi, and Steve formalize an agreement known as JANS. The group aims to work toward the final four, but its existence is not the whole merge: Harry, Justin, John, Cody, Allix, Katie, and others are still making decisions with their own relationships and goals.

title: John and Cody leave the game
description: Split Tribals eliminate John and Cody at the final ten. A smaller voting pool and the Touchy Subjects challenge sharpen the risks around alliances and individual reputation.

story.heading: One game, two councils
story.body: The merged group is split for separate votes, changing who can actually help whom. John and Cody are eliminated. The outcome depends on the people in each voting group rather than one season-wide majority.

story.heading: The social picture becomes more visible
story.body: The Touchy Subjects challenge offers a different kind of information: how players are perceived by their peers. As the field gets smaller, public impressions can affect whether someone is seen as a valuable ally, a possible finalist, or a target.

story.heading: Ponderosa begins
story.body: The first Ponderosa recording follows these eliminations. From here onward, each exit shapes a jury whose judgment will eventually have direct consequences for the finalists’ football rosters.

title: Justin is eliminated
description: Justin is voted out at final eight. With idols, advantages, and potential splits in play, players have to account for both the votes they can see and the protections they cannot.

story.heading: Eight players, limited room for error
story.body: By final eight, the field contains people with competing past loyalties and a growing number of reasons to guard information. Prospective targets cannot assume that everyone publicly agreeing on a plan will vote the same way.

story.heading: Advantages keep the vote unsettled
story.body: Idols, possible extra votes, and the need to anticipate protection make straightforward numbers less reliable. Justin becomes the person eliminated, but the week’s strategic tension extends to other players who are trying to hold relationships together or find a safer route forward.

story.heading: Every exit adds another perspective
story.body: Justin joins Ponderosa. The jury will not simply evaluate who survived each Tribal; its members will bring their own experiences of the game into the final vote.

title: Harry’s torch goes out
description: Harry goes home at final seven, ending the story currently covered by the produced episodes. The vote turns on perceived threats, football strength, and competing visions of the late-game field.

story.heading: A dangerous point in the game
story.body: Harry has built relationships and fields a roster viewed as capable of winning key football contests. That makes him a serious consideration as the field narrows, particularly when a single immunity result can deny other players a choice.

story.heading: Different targets, different incentives
story.body: Harry, Allix, and Katie become part of the wider conversation about who should remain for the final six and five. Players weigh immunity potential, relationships, jury prospects, and the possibility that an advantage changes the vote. JANS members have their own disagreements about the preferred route, while people outside that group continue protecting their interests.

story.heading: The edited episodes end here
story.body: Harry is voted out. The auction also belongs to this phase, and Produced Episode 11 covers this elimination. The rest of the season is documented through individual Tribal recordings, Ponderosa, and player confessionals, with no unreleased episodes presented as finished content.

title: Allix is voted out
description: Allix is eliminated at final six. Older relationships, hidden commitments, and advantage uncertainty make the late-game vote difficult to read from the outside.

story.heading: The remaining relationships overlap
story.body: Allix has longstanding connections dating to the earliest tribes and remains an active part of the endgame conversations. Katie is also looking for a viable path, while Aly, Navi, Joel, and Steve are each balancing relationships and commitments that do not all point in the same direction.

story.heading: A vote with consequences beyond this week
story.body: Advantage questions and potential vote splits matter at final six. Players weigh not only who can survive the next Tribal but also which remaining competitors would be difficult to face in jury deliberations or fantasy scoring. Allix is ultimately eliminated.

story.heading: The calendar accelerates
story.body: The next stage compresses the usual fantasy and Tribal rhythm around Thanksgiving. Everyone left has less time to adjust lineups, gather information, and decide whom they want beside them at the end.

title: A special weekend Tribal
description: A compressed Thanksgiving schedule leads to Katie’s elimination at final five. The remaining four players are Aly, Navi, Joel, and Steve, but the season is not decided by an alliance agreement.

story.heading: A different kind of football week
story.body: Thursday–Friday games and Sunday–Monday games count as separate scoring windows, requiring quick roster decisions and leaving little time between competitive results and Tribal planning.

story.heading: Katie looks for an opening
story.body: As the only player outside the four-person JANS agreement at final five, Katie is seeking a route through a difficult vote. Relationships built earlier in the season still matter, and the remaining group must decide whether to hold the agreement or change course for the final stage.

story.heading: The final four is set
story.body: Katie is voted out. Aly, Navi, Joel, and Steve reach final four, fulfilling a common objective, but only three can advance. From this point each person has to consider the endgame on individual terms.

title: One last elimination
description: Aly wins final immunity, and Joel becomes the final eliminated player. Aly, Navi, and Steve advance to a jury decision that will determine their championship roster additions.

story.heading: Immunity changes the final decision
story.body: Aly wins the last immunity competition. The final-four vote therefore falls on the remaining options, and the alliance that survived the late game cannot stay intact.

story.heading: Joel goes to the jury
story.body: Joel is eliminated at the final-four Tribal. Each finalist now arrives with a different route through the tribes, merge, and endgame. The question shifts from who is safe to how the jury will evaluate those paths.

story.heading: The last events before the final
story.body: Fallen Comrades and the final Ponderosa recording accompany this phase. The archive indexes the final-four Tribal and related footage, but the separate final-three Tribal recording is not among the supplied assets.

title: The jury and the fantasy final
description: The jury makes its decision, then fantasy football determines the season winner across NFL Weeks 14 and 15.

story.heading: Final Tribal
story.body: Aly, Navi, and Steve reach the final three by different routes through the game. At the jury vote, Aly receives five votes, Navi three, and Steve none. Rather than crowning a winner directly, each jury vote gives the finalist that juror’s two best fantasy football players to use in a two-week championship.

story.heading: The final two football weeks
story.body: The first week is close at the top: Steve scores 186.6, Aly 182.74, and Navi 113.06. With another slate of NFL games ahead, the outcome remains open. By the end of Week 15, Steve has the highest combined score and wins the season, with Aly second and Navi third. The screenshots below preserve the actual fantasy results.

story.heading: The end of the season
story.body: The final three were shaped by different social relationships, immunity outcomes, and fantasy rosters. The jury mattered because it changed which players were available for the football final; the fantasy results decided the championship. The remaining confessionals offer a final look back at the season.
